text: A CI/CD pipeline is an automated workload with no human at the keyboard during the run, but it still needs to authenticate to deploy infrastructure or push a container image. For years the default was generating a cloud credential and dropping it into the pipeline's secrets store — and that credential becomes one of the highest-value targets in the whole enterprise.

That stored secret usually sits there for the life of the pipeline, often with far broader permissions than any single run actually needs, copyable by anyone with admin access to the CI/CD platform itself. A leaked pipeline secret is arguably worse than a leaked human password — it typically has standing permission to touch production directly, with no MFA prompt in the way.

Managed identity is the cloud-native fix for resources running inside your cloud: an identity assigned directly to that resource by the platform itself. Code simply asks the platform's metadata endpoint for a token when it needs one, and the platform issues and rotates it automatically. There's no secret in a config file, because that kind of credential never exists in a form a human could copy.

A pipeline that runs on the CI/CD vendor's own infrastructure has no cloud resource to attach a managed identity to — that's what OIDC federation solves. The CI/CD platform already issues a short-lived token asserting facts like which repo and branch triggered the run, the cloud platform trusts that issuer, and it exchanges that token for its own short-lived access token. No stored secret ever changes hands.

Both mechanisms replace a shared secret, which leaks if either side is compromised, with federated trust verified cryptographically on every single request. It's Chapter 2's continuous-verification philosophy, now applied to the workloads that deploy everything else — the same zero-trust principle this course has given to people, extended to pipelines and scripts.

Next lesson extends zero trust one step further — to SaaS applications that live entirely outside your own infrastructure, where neither a managed identity nor a federated pipeline token has any direct path to reach.
